question: Can a neural network be understood as a mixture of path-wise simple experts, and can a deep linearly gated surrogate expose feature learning as the movement of half-space intersections and explain why optimization allocates more active paths to simpler target-function regions?

key_findings.claim: The path-wise mixture-of-experts decomposition of a ReLU network is an exact and useful algebraic reframing.
key_findings.evidence: A path is active when every ReLU gate along it is on, and its expert value is the product of path weights times a linear function of the input. Summing active path values recovers the ordinary network output; the appendix proves this by expanding layer recurrences. This cleanly separates binary path activity from path value, although it does not by itself explain training or generalization.

anchors.section: The ReLU Network as a Mixture of Simple Experts, Equations 2-3 and Theorem 1

key_findings.claim: DLGN creates a particularly simple geometric gate family: every gate is a half-space in the original input, so each active path is an intersection of at most depth-many half-spaces.
key_findings.evidence: The gating stream is a deep linear map eta_l(x)=W_l eta_{l-1}(x), while a separate U stream carries expert values through the resulting binary masks. Because every eta_l,i is ultimately linear in x, each neuron cuts the original input with one hyperplane and every path region is a convex polyhedron. The piecewise-constant variant replaces the value stream's input by ones, leaving a sum of constant experts over polyhedral regions.

anchors.section: Deep Linearly Gated Network, Equations 4-5 and Theorem 2

key_findings.claim: The paper presents DLGN as a proposed model without acknowledging that essentially the same architecture and interpretation had already been introduced by the same research line.
key_findings.evidence: The text says it proposes and names the Deep Linearly Gated Network, but its references include only the authors' 2020 neural-path work. Primary records from 2021 and 2022 already define DLGN as a deep linear feature/gating network whose masks drive a separate value network, motivate its primal and dual linearities, and report CIFAR-10/100 comparisons. The 2024 paper's incremental contribution is therefore the active-region visualization and resource-allocation story, not the DLGN architecture itself.

anchors.section: Overview and Mixture of Simple Experts Framework

key_findings.claim: As mathematically specified, the hard-gated DLGN has no ordinary gradient signal for learning its gating parameters, yet the paper never states the surrogate used to produce the claimed moving half-spaces.
key_findings.evidence: The only dependence of the prediction on W is through indicators 1[eta_l,i(x)>=0]. Their derivative with respect to W is zero almost everywhere and undefined at a boundary. The experiments simply say the models were optimized with Adam; there is no straight-through estimator, sigmoid relaxation, auxiliary loss, or other gate-gradient rule in the full text. Consequently, the core empirical statement that gradient-based training moves DLGN half-spaces is not reproducible from the displayed model. A later DLGN paper explicitly replaces indicators with a sigmoid during training, underscoring that this missing choice is material.

anchors.section: Deep Linearly Gated Network, Equation 4 and Theorem 2

key_findings.claim: The overlap kernel is a readable co-activation statistic, but it is not a complete measure of the features or capacity used by the actual DLGN.
key_findings.evidence: Lambda(x,x') counts paths simultaneously active for two inputs and factorizes into products of jointly active neuron counts. The linear-kernel equivalence invoked in its motivation assumes constant expert values that can be independently optimized. In the implemented DLGN, exponentially many path values share multiplicative U parameters and are neither independent nor equally important. Lambda ignores expert magnitude, sign, cancellation, parameter sharing, and output sensitivity, so a bright heatmap cell is gate multiplicity rather than demonstrated predictive resource.

anchors.section: Deep Linearly Gated Network and Piecewise Constant DLGN

key_findings.claim: On the circle toy problem, learned-gate DLGN and ReLU models converge far faster than a frozen-gate DLGN and show early gate-count concentration on the low-frequency half.
key_findings.evidence: The five-layer, width-16 models fit a target with low frequency on the top semicircle and high frequency on the bottom. DLGN and ReLU reach loss below 0.01 in roughly 200 epochs, whereas frozen-gate DLGN takes more than 2,000 epochs and still shows artifacts after 8,000. Trace-normalized overlap and NTK heatmaps change by epoch 3, and more paths become active on the low-frequency half. This is suggestive evidence that adaptive gates help this constructed task, conditional on the unspecified gate-gradient implementation.

anchors.section: Neural Network Feature Learning and Figure 2

key_findings.claim: The frozen-gate ablation establishes that one random finite feature map optimizes more slowly, not that feature learning is generally necessary for efficient neural-network learning.
key_findings.evidence: Only one width, depth, initialization regime, optimizer, and hand-designed frequency task are shown, with no tuned random-feature width, learned linear head with independent path coefficients, NTK regression, or equal-parameter kernel baseline. Freezing the W stream changes optimization while U still has a highly shared deep multiplicative parameterization. The observed gap is real for the displayed setup but does not isolate whether it arises from adaptive representation, conditioning, finite random-feature coverage, or the value-network parameterization.

key_findings.claim: The claim that gradient descent allocates resources preferentially to simpler regions is an interesting hypothesis, not a controlled or quantified result.
key_findings.evidence: On modified FashionMNIST, classes 1-5 retain semantic labels while classes 6-10 are replaced by randomly assigned labels over 25 unspecified clusters. The paper plots more active paths for the former group and calls this an innate weakness of gradient descent. But the two halves differ in label construction, geometry, margin, noise, and learnability; path count is exponentially sensitive to layerwise activation rates; and no normalization by region mass, class balance, confidence, gradient magnitude, or required approximation complexity is provided. The appendix averages three runs but supplies no numeric estimates or uncertainty bars.

anchors.section: Modified FashionMNIST and Gradient Descent as a Resource Allocator

key_findings.claim: The DLGN evidence does not support the paper's extrapolation that ordinary ReLU networks learn the same half-space-intersection features or allocation mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: A ReLU neuron's later-layer gate is a nonlinear, piecewise-linear function of the input, and an active path region can be disconnected, whereas every DLGN gate is a global input-space half-space. The argument for transfer consists of broadly similar toy heatmaps and modestly similar CIFAR accuracy. There is no mapping between learned DLGN and ReLU regions, intervention on corresponding paths, quantitative region-similarity metric, or proof that ReLU NTK evolution is caused by path-region movement rather than changes in path values and activation magnitudes.

key_findings.claim: Accuracy comparisons are not capacity- or compute-matched and give mixed evidence that DLGN is comparable to ReLU networks.
key_findings.evidence: At the same nominal widths and depths, DLGN uses separate W and U parameter sets while ReLU uses one, yet parameter counts and runtime are not reported. In the small five-convolution experiment, ReLU, DLGN, and DLGN-PWC test accuracies are 72.17%, 73.2%, and 72.2%, but their training accuracies differ sharply and the unexplained DLGN test accuracy exceeds its train accuracy. In ResNet-34/110 tables, DLGN trails ReLU by 5-6 percentage points on both CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 despite the extra stream. No modern tuned baseline or uncertainty is given.

key_findings.claim: The paper repeatedly attributes the phenomenon to gradient descent while every disclosed experiment uses Adam.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion calls path concentration an automatic consequence and innate weakness of gradient descent and bases its mechanism story on first-order gradient dynamics. The appendix lists Adam with learning rate 2e-4 for both CIFAR and FashionMNIST; no plain-GD or SGD experiment is reported. Adam rescales coordinates using moment estimates, so the observations cannot be directly assigned to gradient descent without an optimizer ablation or an explicit broader definition.

anchors.section: Gradient Descent as a Resource Allocator

key_findings.claim: The two proved theorems certify only forward-pass identities; the central learning, interpretability, clustering, and optimization claims have no theorem or statistical test.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 expands a ReLU forward pass into path products, and Theorem 2 performs the analogous expansion for DLGN. The appendix proofs are induction and index rearrangement. There is no result showing gate learnability, convergence, half-space alignment with smooth target regions, preferential resource allocation, superiority to fixed kernels, fidelity to ReLU dynamics, or generalization. Those claims rest on visual inspection of a toy problem and a small set of accuracy tables.

key_findings.claim: Reproducibility is insufficient for the main visual and accuracy claims.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix gives layer counts, widths, Adam, and one learning rate, but not epochs, batch size, initialization, losses, preprocessing/augmentation, train/test transforms, weight decay, learning-rate schedule, gate relaxation, random seeds, selection rules, exact modified-Fashion clustering, random relabeling, or ResNet conversion details. No code or artifact locator appears in the cached paper. Main tables appear to be single estimates, while three-run Fashion plots omit numerical values and uncertainty.

method.core_idea: View a deep network as a sum over path experts, then replace ReLU's recursively nonlinear gates by a deep-linear gating stream so every learned gate is a globally visualizable half-space while a separate value stream retains nonlinear piecewise prediction capacity.
method.mechanism: For each path, multiply binary neuron gates to define its active input region and multiply value-stream weights to define its linear or constant expert. Sum all active expert outputs efficiently through ordinary layered computation. Define an overlap kernel by counting paths co-active for input pairs, visualize its evolution and half-space gates during training, compare adaptive and frozen gating on a two-frequency circle task, and measure path counts on a deliberately simple-versus-complex FashionMNIST relabeling. Compare DLGN, PWC-DLGN, ReLU, deep-linear, and ResNet variants on CIFAR accuracy.
assumptions: The displayed hard indicators receive a useful gradient under the unspecified implementation.
A deep linearly gated network is a faithful enough surrogate to infer ReLU feature-learning mechanisms.
Co-active path count is proportional to effective predictive resources despite shared value parameters.
Trace-normalized overlap-kernel brightness identifies task-relevant learned features.
Low target frequency on a circle and ordinary semantic Fashion classes are adequate definitions of simple regions.
Randomly relabeled clusters create a controlled complexity intervention without introducing label noise or geometric confounds.
A frozen finite random gate network is a representative fixed-kernel baseline.
Same width and depth make DLGN and ReLU comparisons fair despite separate W and U streams.
Adam observations reveal an optimizer-independent property of gradient descent.
Visual similarity of overlap and NTK heatmaps implies a common causal feature-learning mechanism.
Path regions can be treated as distinct experts or resources even though they share parameters multiplicatively.
Results on one low-dimensional regression construction and modified FashionMNIST extend to general neural feature learning.

techniques.role: Rewrites the network prediction as a sum of active path expert values.
Produces every gate from a linear function of the original input.
Carries learned path values through masks generated by the gating stream.
Feeds ones to the value stream so active paths contribute constant experts.
Represents a path's domain as the intersection of its active neuron regions.
Counts paths simultaneously active for each input pair.
Compares adaptive gates with random gates fixed at initialization.
Creates adjacent low- and high-frequency target regions for visual analysis.
Contrasts ordinary semantic classes with a more complex randomly relabeled cluster partition.
Visualizes overlap and empirical NTK structure over training.

evaluations.setting: Two-dimensional unit-circle regression with low target frequency on one semicircle and high frequency on the other, using five-layer width-16 ReLU, DLGN, and frozen-gate DLGN
evaluations.metric: Squared-loss curves, trace-normalized overlap and empirical-NTK heatmaps, predicted curves, and visualized DLGN half-spaces at initialization, epoch 3, and late training
evaluations.result: Adaptive DLGN and ReLU reach low loss in about 200 epochs, frozen-gate DLGN needs over 2,000, and active-path mass concentrates early on the low-frequency semicircle
evaluations.baseline: Only one frozen random-gate configuration; no width-matched random features, exact NTK regression, independent path-value model, plain gradient descent, or uncertainty across seeds

evaluations.setting: Modified FashionMNIST in which classes 1-5 remain semantic labels and classes 6-10 are produced by clustering the latter five original classes into 25 groups and randomly reassigning five labels
evaluations.metric: Average active-path counts, empirical NTK diagonal, test accuracy, and class-averaged 10-by-10 overlap/NTK heatmaps over three runs
evaluations.result: DLGN and ReLU allocate more active paths to the ordinary-label half than to the cluster-relabelled half, which the paper interprets as preferential resources for easier regions
evaluations.baseline: No controlled complexity continuum, cluster-definition report, region-mass normalization, label-noise control, numeric effect sizes, confidence intervals, or optimizer ablation

evaluations.setting: Five-convolution-layer CIFAR-10 comparison at nominally matched layer/filter counts
evaluations.result: ReLU reports 96.3% train and 72.17% test; DLGN 85.3% and 73.2%; DLGN-PWC 84.9% and 72.2%; deep linear 42.3% and 40.79%
evaluations.baseline: Nominal architecture matching only; separate DLGN parameter streams, gate training rule, preprocessing, uncertainty, runtime, and parameter counts are not controlled

evaluations.setting: ResNet-34 and ResNet-110 variants on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
evaluations.result: All variants report 100% train accuracy; DLGN trails ReLU by 5 points on CIFAR-10 for both depths and by about 5.1-6 points on CIFAR-100
evaluations.baseline: ReLU ResNets are included, but the DLGN conversion, optimization recipe, parameter/compute matching, seeds, and stronger kernel or interpretable-model baselines are absent

limitations: DLGN had already been introduced in 2021/2022 work from the same research line, which the paper does not cite.
The hard indicator gates have zero gradients almost everywhere, and the paper never specifies how W is trained.
The overlap kernel counts gates but ignores path-value magnitude, sign, cancellation, and parameter sharing.
The claimed kernel equivalence assumes independently optimized expert constants, unlike the multiplicatively shared DLGN value stream.
Active paths are not independent experts or capacity units because exponentially many share the same neuron and edge parameters.
The circle result uses one hand-designed two-dimensional target, one architecture, and no seed uncertainty.
The frozen-gate comparison lacks competitive random-feature and exact-kernel baselines.
Modified FashionMNIST changes label semantics, geometry, clustering, and noise simultaneously rather than isolating complexity.
The clustering algorithm and random relabeling protocol are not specified.
No quantitative metric validates later-layer clustering or half-space alignment with smooth target regions.
Only four of sixteen final-layerwise circle gates are highlighted in the main visualization.
ReLU and DLGN active regions have fundamentally different geometry, weakening surrogate claims.
DLGN has separate gate and value parameters but comparisons do not match parameter count or compute.
The ResNet DLGN variants lag ReLU by 5-6 accuracy points and lack architecture details.
All disclosed optimizers are Adam despite claims specifically about gradient descent.
Theorems establish forward identities only, not learning dynamics, convergence, generalization, or resource allocation.
The CIFAR tables have no seeds, deviations, preprocessing details, tuned baselines, or wall-clock measurements.
No code, exact artifact locator, or complete training configuration is given in the cached paper.
The unexplained small-CIFAR DLGN train/test relationship complicates interpretation of Table 1.
No natural task tests whether half-space visualizations support a faithful human prediction or debugging decision.
failure_modes: The implemented hard gate receives zero gradient and remains at initialization despite being described as learned.
A hidden straight-through or soft-gate rule materially changes the architecture and learned geometry across implementations.
Overlap heatmaps brighten because activation rates change, even when the corresponding paths have negligible or canceling values.
Exponential path multiplicity amplifies a small neuron-level activation imbalance into an apparent large resource-allocation effect.
The frozen-gate model is underparameterized in effective random features and makes adaptation look necessary.
The model learns the low-frequency circle half first due to ordinary spectral bias rather than path-region motion causing NTK improvement.
Modified FashionMNIST path allocation tracks class margin, density, or label noise instead of target simplicity.
A DLGN half-space appears interpretable globally but its effect on output is unfaithful because many shared path values cancel it.
ReLU networks achieve similar heatmaps for a different mechanistic reason, invalidating transfer from the DLGN surrogate.
Doubling parameter streams gives DLGN an unfair small-model advantage while still failing to match ReLU at ResNet scale.
Adam-specific coordinate rescaling drives gate concentration that disappears under SGD or full-batch gradient descent.
The later-layer normal vectors collapse or become redundant because deep-linear matrix products are ill-conditioned.
Bias-free global half-spaces cannot express task-relevant affine partitions unless the untested constant-node construction works in the target architecture.
Trace normalization hides collapse in the absolute number or diversity of active paths.
Visual selection of representative neurons overstates clustering relative to all neurons and seeds.
reusable_insights: Path-wise algebra can separate gating decisions from value computation and produce exact model decompositions.
When claiming gate learning, specify and ablate the differentiable relaxation or estimator used for hard thresholds.
Distinguish active-path count from effective capacity by weighting paths with output influence, gradients, or causal ablations.
Compare gate-only overlap with the value-weighted kernel, empirical NTK, and intervention-based feature importance.
Match parameter count, FLOPs, optimizer, schedule, and tuning budget when comparing separate-stream and ordinary networks.
Use exact NTK regression, wide random features, learned independent heads, and frozen-gate networks as distinct baselines.
Create a controlled target-complexity continuum while matching input density, class margin, label noise, and sample count.
Normalize resource measures by region probability and report neuron-level as well as exponentially expanded path-level quantities.
Validate a surrogate by mapping interventions and predictions between surrogate and target model, not by accuracy or heatmap resemblance alone.
Separate early spectral learning, gate movement, value learning, and optimizer conditioning through factorial ablations.
Quantify geometric claims with hyperplane angles, region overlap, boundary distance, clustering scores, and seed uncertainty.
Test whether an interpretation predicts counterfactual effects when gates or paths are removed, rotated, or reassigned.
State novelty against the authors' own prior architecture papers and isolate the genuinely new analysis layer.
Use plain gradient descent or phrase conclusions as optimizer-generic first-order observations when experiments use Adam.
Publish executable architecture definitions because a one-line choice between a step, ReLU, sigmoid, and straight-through gate changes the learning mechanism.
open_questions: What differentiable gate or gradient estimator was actually used to train W in every reported DLGN experiment?
Do the results persist under exact hard gates at inference after systematically varying sigmoid temperature or straight-through rules?
How much of the overlap-kernel signal remains after weighting paths by learned value and causal output contribution?
Can path capacity be defined without exponentially double-counting parameters shared across paths?
Does adaptive gating still beat exact NTK regression and width-matched random features at equal parameter and compute budgets?
Are circle results stable across target frequencies, rotations, noise, widths, depths, seeds, and optimizers?
Can simple and complex regions be varied while holding density, margin, noise, and class semantics fixed?
Does the resource-allocation direction reverse when the hard region carries more probability mass or higher loss weight?
What quantitative correspondence exists between DLGN half-spaces and ReLU active-path regions trained on the same data?
Do gate interventions that matter in DLGN identify causally important ReLU circuits?
How do deep-linear product conditioning and implicit bias affect later-layer half-space normals?
Can a value-aware visualization retain global readability while exposing sign, magnitude, and cancellation?
Do DLGN interpretations help humans predict failures or improve models on a blinded task?
Which contribution remains novel relative to the 2021 and 2022 DLGN papers after matching architectures and experiments?
Why does the small CIFAR DLGN report test accuracy above training accuracy, and what exact evaluation modes/transforms were used?
Can the claimed gradient-descent mechanism be proven even in a two-layer soft-gated DLGN?

competitive_landscape.title: Disentangling deep neural networks with rectified linear units using duality
competitive_landscape.difference: This same research line already introduces DLGN as a deep-linear preactivation/gating network masking a separate value network, describes primal and dual linearities, and evaluates CIFAR-10/100. It makes the 2024 architecture claim incremental; the newer paper chiefly adds active-path regions, overlap visualizations, and the simple-region allocation hypothesis.

competitive_landscape.title: Explicitising The Implicit Intrepretability of Deep Neural Networks Via Duality
competitive_landscape.difference: This follow-up already motivates DLGN by making the feature network linear, feeding ones to the value network, and studying an interpretability-accuracy tradeoff on CIFAR. The piecewise-constant and disentanglement elements in Half-Space Feature Learning therefore have substantial direct precedent.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Path Features and Neural Path Kernel : Understanding the role of gates in deep learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Lakshminarayanan and Singh already encode ReLU gate states as neural path features, separate neural path values, define the neural path kernel, and show learned gates matter on MNIST/CIFAR. The 2024 overlap kernel is a closely related co-activation count specialized to its MoE framing and DLGN geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Networks as Kernel Learners: The Silent Alignment Effect
competitive_landscape.difference: Silent alignment gives a quantitative mechanism in which an evolving tangent kernel learns eigenstructure early and later grows in scale, with analytical treatment for homogeneous linear networks and explicit initialization/data conditions. Half-Space Feature Learning offers a geometric path-gate narrative but does not establish that gate motion causes the observed NTK evolution.

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Regularization via Neural Feature Alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: Baratin et al. quantify tangent-feature alignment and compression toward task-relevant directions along optimization paths. It provides spectral and complexity measures against which the DLGN paper's qualitative trace-normalized overlap heatmaps should be compared.

competitive_landscape.title: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang and Hu classify parameterizations into feature-learning and kernel regimes and derive computable infinite-width feature-learning limits. This replaces the paper's two-extremes setup with a formal continuum and shows that feature learning is not inherently a finite-width phenomenon.

competitive_landscape.title: A Theoretical Analysis on Feature Learning in Neural Networks: Emergence from Inputs and Advantage over Fixed Features
competitive_landscape.difference: Shi, Wei, and Liang prove emergence of effective features from structured inputs and a separation from polynomial-size data-independent features. The DLGN paper cites this direction but offers only visual evidence on a toy target and no analogous learning or sample-complexity guarantee.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Networks can Learn Representations with Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: Damian, Lee, and Soltanolkotabi prove that gradient descent on a two-layer network learns low-dimensional relevant directions with better sample complexity and transfer than kernel methods for a broad polynomial family. Half-Space Feature Learning seeks a more visual multilayer mechanism but does not demonstrate a controlled advantage over a tuned kernel baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: How Does Gradient Descent Learn Features -- A Local Analysis for Regularized Two-Layer Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou and Ge prove ground-truth direction recovery both early and after loss becomes small under an explicit regularized objective. It demonstrates the kind of optimization theorem and late-stage control missing from the DLGN resource-allocation conjecture.

competitive_landscape.title: How Feature Learning Can Improve Neural Scaling Laws
competitive_landscape.difference: Bordelon, Atanasov, and Pehlevan formalize hard, easy, and super-easy targets by membership in the initial NTK RKHS and show analytically when feature learning changes compute scaling exponents. This supplies an operational task-difficulty definition and scaling tests absent from the paper's frequency/cluster labels.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Networks Learn Features From Local Discontinuities in the Label Function
competitive_landscape.difference: The later ICLR 2025 work develops DLGN with explicit sigmoid relaxation for trainable gates, formalizes label-function discontinuity scores, adds architecture variants and decision-tree extraction, and evaluates broader binary tasks. It both extends the half-space hypothesis and exposes the 2024 paper's missing hard-gate training specification.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a novel mixture-of-simple-experts viewpoint and DLGN model that make neural features globally visualizable as path regions formed by intersections of input-space half-spaces, revealing preferential allocation toward simpler target regions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact ReLU path expansion, active-path-region terminology, overlap-kernel visualization, circle dynamics, and modified-Fashion resource-allocation observation form a coherent analysis package. However, neural path features/kernels and the DLGN architecture were already published by the same line of work, while broader NTK-alignment and feature-learning theory predates this paper.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is the particular geometric visualization and simple-region allocation hypothesis, not DLGN or path gating. The evidence remains exploratory because the displayed hard gates are not differentiably trainable without an unstated mechanism, overlap counts are not value-aware resources, comparisons are not matched, the ReLU transfer is unvalidated, and central claims have neither controlled statistics nor theory.

reviewer_notes: Primary review covered all 21 cached pages, including every main and appendix figure, the two algebraic proofs, all accuracy tables, and disclosed hyperparameters. Competitive research used primary arXiv and OpenReview records through 2026-08-23. The highest-priority verification item is the actual DLGN gate implementation: the written step indicators cannot learn W by ordinary backpropagation, and no estimator or relaxation appears anywhere in the artifact. A secondary reviewer should obtain code, reproduce the gate-gradient path, check original revision chronology against the uncited 2021/2022 DLGN papers, recompute overlap with value/gradient weighting, and rerun the toy and Fashion experiments with exact NTK/random-feature baselines, matched parameter budgets, plain SGD/GD, quantitative geometry metrics, and preregistered seeds.
